321	The highest knowledge of man, the highest awareness
322	of man, was in calling the names
323	according to their truth.
324	And his fall is seen in the blurring of the names.
325	The name shows the essence of the thing.
326	The name points to the essence of the thing.
327	Calling the names according to their truth means grasping the essence fully,
328	and then man's knowledge is whole.
329	When the names are blurred,
330	then man's knowledge is blurred,
331	damaged.
332	"Know the God of your father."
333	How do we know Him?
334	It is written, "those who know Your name."
335	We can know Him, recognize Him, only through His names.
336	And the name shows the essence of the thing.
337	The names are the paths to grasping Divinity.
338	They are called the paths to grasping Divinity.
339	Each name shows the way to grasp Divinity at that level, according to that level.
340	Every spiritual level, worlds too.
341	There are partzufim, sefirot, every level essentially has a name, which means
342	a revelation of Divinity, according to that level.
343	Another kind of revelation of Divinity.
344	And what is the purpose of Creation?
345	To know the world; the Holy One, blessed be He, created the world.
346	The Zohar says, "so that they will know," that we recognize Him, that we know Him.
347	All His paths of revelation, which appear in a name through the names.
348	So a person cannot have knowledge of the Creator, "know the God of your father," without full recognition of the names.
349	Because it gets blurred, it gets blurred.
350	It is impossible to raise the spirit as long as the fundamental names do not stand
351	in lowliness.
352	The divine names need to be explained according to their highest exaltedness.
353	And with them all their appellations will be explained.
354	We must study the names, we must explain the names.
355	And all the names, behold,
356	need to be explained according to their highest exaltedness, and with them all their appellations will be explained.
357	And all the names of the spiritual branches, of feeling, of thought,
358	of action, that relate to them.
359	Everything must come out of distress, lowliness and contempt, which folly has cast over them,
